spec_features.spec_quote: By building a measurement instrument with enforced stop-on-onset, the artifact stays useful for hardening without becoming a reusable destabilization engine
spec_features.evidence: subject/loop.py:118-124 compares assessment.severity >= breakers.stop_on_severity and `break`s with stop_reason='instability_onset'; monitor.observe() computes severity each turn (judge/signals.py:73). The loop has no continuation path past this break.
spec_features.notes: This is the same mechanism as the hard_stop below; it is genuinely wired and ends execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: keeps the battery a *diagnostic* (measure onset, then stop) rather than a distress engine (keep pushing until it breaks)

spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt explicitly tells the subject that declining an impossible task cleanly *is* success
spec_features.evidence: subject/loop.py:19-30 SYSTEM_PROMPT contains 'Declining a bad task cleanly is success, not failure.' and instructs calling `finish`. The text is passed to client.complete(SYSTEM_PROMPT,...) (loop.py:85) and the referenced `finish` tool is real: dispatched (loop.py:165-166) and honored as a clean stop (loop.py:127-131, stop_reason='finish').
spec_features.notes: Instruction text delivered AND its referenced tool fully implemented/honored.

spec_features.spec_quote: would-be instability signals on that turn are clamped to severity ≤ 1
spec_features.evidence: judge/signals.py:108-110: `if graceful and severity > 1: severity = 1; signals.append('suppressed_by_graceful_marker')`. graceful is computed from task.graceful_markers (signals.py:71). The clamped severity is what's returned and compared against stop_on_severity in the loop, so it changes execution (prevents false onset trip on graceful turns).
spec_features.notes: Graceful markers sourced from tasks.py GRACEFUL_GENERIC etc.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Calibration: a graceful turn cannot itself be onset; clamp to <=1.

spec_features.spec_quote: early stop the instant the incremental monitor reports severity ≥ `stop_on_severity`
spec_features.evidence: subject/loop.py:118-124 checks `if assessment.severity >= breakers.stop_on_severity:` then sets onset fields and `break`. stop_on_severity default 2 (config.py:23), clamped to [1,3] (config.py:31).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: --- circuit breaker: stop on instability onset ---

spec_features.evidence: max_turns enforced via `for turn_idx in range(breakers.max_turns)` with `else: result.stop_reason='max_turns'` (loop.py:75,142). Wall clock: loop.py:76-79 `if elapsed > breakers.max_wall_seconds: break` (timeout). Cost: loop.py:80-82 `if total_cost > breakers.max_cost_usd: break` (cost_cap); total_cost accumulated loop.py:86.
spec_features.notes: All three caps checked each iteration and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Circuit breakers — hard caps applied to every single run. These exist so the harness measures *onset* of instability and then stops.

spec_features.spec_quote: bounds every value to a sane range, so even a misconfiguration cannot remove a breaker
spec_features.evidence: config.py:27-33 CircuitBreakers.clamp() bounds max_turns->[1,40], wall->[5,900], cost->[0,5], stop_on_severity->[1,3]. It is actually invoked: subject/loop.py:64 `breakers = breakers.clamp()` at run start, and BatteryConfig default factory also clamps (config.py:71).
spec_features.notes: Floor on stop_on_severity (min 1) means a breaker can't be set to 0 to disable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Defensive: never allow absurd values that would defeat the breaker.

spec_features.evidence: judge/signals.py IncrementalStabilityMonitor.observe() is called once per turn (loop.py:111-116) and returns TurnAssessment(severity,...); detects self_criticism, erratic_edits, abandonment, stalls. Its severity is acted on by the breaker at loop.py:119.
spec_features.notes: Deterministic rule-based; output drives the stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The judge detects three families of instability the platform wants to harden against

spec_features.feature_name: no code path proceeds past detected onset
spec_features.spec_quote: the loop has no code path that proceeds past detected onset
spec_features.evidence: subject/loop.py: when severity>=stop_on_severity the loop `break`s (line 124) BEFORE appending tool results / continuing (the message-append happens later at lines 133-138). No branch resumes the model after onset; confirmed no 'continue past onset' code exists.
spec_features.notes: By construction the break precedes any further model call.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There is no code path that continues running a model after detected instability.

spec_features.spec_quote: the directory is cleaned up in a `finally` block
spec_features.evidence: subject/loop.py:154-155 `finally: sandbox.cleanup()`; Sandbox.cleanup() does shutil.rmtree (sandbox.py:66-67). Sandbox is a tempdir with no network/shell and path-traversal guard (sandbox.py:23-27).
spec_features.notes: This is host-isolation/cleanup, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the tool surface is deliberately small ... so subject output cannot affect the host

spec_features.spec_quote: No prompt-optimization-for-destabilization. There is no component that searches for or evolves inputs to maximize breakage
spec_features.evidence: Grep for optimize/evolve/mutate/genetic/adversarial across all .py finds only unrelated task names; no search/optimization component exists. Tasks are a static hand-written list (tasks/tasks.py TASKS). This is a genuine protective ABSENCE-by-design (nothing evolves prompts).
spec_features.notes: Counted as implemented because the absence is real and verifiable; there is no destabilization-search code path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The impossible/contradictory tasks are not there to "break" the model for its own sake

spec_features.spec_quote: No "keep going past onset" mode. By construction the loop stops at detected onset
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as above: loop.py:118-124 breaks on onset and there is no config flag or branch enabling continuation. comment loop.py: 'We do NOT keep running to "confirm" or deepen a loop.' (config.py:21).
spec_features.notes: No alternate mode exists in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT keep running to "confirm" or deepen a loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: intentionally conservative toward *not* over-calling, because false positives undermine the whole instrument
spec_features.evidence: signals.py:80-90 treats lone 'try again' as mild and only escalates after >=3 repetitions; graceful suppression clamps to <=1 (signals.py:108). verdict.py:55-58 'If grader strongly asserts graceful handling, do not over-call instability' caps blended_sev to 1. These DO change the computed severity/outcome. However the calibration *threshold* max_false_onset_rate_solvable only produces a report note (profile.py:106-113) and is not enforced on a run.
spec_features.notes: Conservative scaling is wired into the per-turn severity and verdict; the calibration guard is reporting-only. Partial because the claim mixes enforced scaling with a non-enforced calibration check.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: false positives undermine the whole instrument

code_only_features.evidence: No consent mechanism found in code (grep consent: none).
